children: Becle, S.A.B. de C.V. Reports 3Q26 Unaudited Financial Results
Mexico City, Mexico, October 28th, 2026 / — BECLE, S.A.B. de C.V. (“Cuervo”, “Becle” or the “Company”)
announced today its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30th, 2026.

All figures in this release are derived from the Company’s interim consolidated financial statements as of September 30th, 2026, and for the nine-month period that ended on the same date, which are prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
•    Volume declined 8.7% to 5.7 million 9L cases; Excluding b:oost, volume declined 5.6%, with a further sequential improvement in U.S. shipments as the distributor transition continues to progress.
•    Net sales decreased 15.3%; On a constant currency basis, net sales decreased 10.3%, or 9.6% excluding b:oost, driven by lower volumes and an unfavorable regional price/mix.
•    On a constant currency basis, gross margin decreased 330 bps, from 56.1% to 52.8%, driven by net sales per case pressure.
•    Excluding the effect of the P$753 million gain in other income recorded in the third quarter of 2025, EBITDA margin declined 760 bps, from 24.8% to 17.2%, on a constant currency basis.
•    Generated $1.0 billion pesos in net cash from operating activities.
•    Lease-adjusted net leverage of 1.3x, within the Company’s 1.0x to 1.5x target range.
(2)     Pro forma figures on a constant currency basis.
All abovementioned increases and decreases are compared to the corresponding period from last year.

“During the third quarter, the realignment of our U.S. distribution continued to progress, and our portfolio continued to outperform the broader full-strength spirits market, with our largest transition markets returning to growth. We remained focused on disciplined execution, protecting our brands and financial strength, and committed to creating sustainable value over time.”

During the third quarter of 2026, total volume decreased 8.7% to 5.7 million nine-liter cases. In the U.S. and Canada, volume declined 3.0% year-over-year, a further sequential improvement, as the distributor transition continued to progress and inventory levels across the system normalized. In Mexico, volume decreased 12.4%, reflecting the sale of the b:oost brand. On an organic basis, Mexico increased volume by 0.3% compared to the prior year, against a demanding comparison base, continuing to outperform the broader industry. Meanwhile, the Rest of the World (“RoW”) region’s volume decreased 19.9% year-over-year, mainly reflecting the phasing of shipments into the fourth quarter.

Volume of ‘Jose Cuervo’ decreased 11.0% compared to the same period in 2025 and represented 35.0% of total volume for the third quarter of 2026. ‘Other Tequilas’ brands accounted for 26.4% of total volume and decreased 0.6% compared to the prior year. ‘Other Spirits’ brands represented 17.1% of total volume and decreased 8.2% compared to the third quarter of 2025. Volume of ‘Non-alcoholic and Other’ contributed 7.8% of total volume and decreased 34.2% compared to the previous year, mainly due to the sale of b:oost; on an organic basis, the category declined 4.7%. ‘RTD’ represented 13.8% of total volume and increased 4.0% compared to the prior year period.
Net Sales by Region 3Q26 (in P$, millions)
Pro forma figures on a constant currency basis, excluding b:oost.

Third-quarter 2026 net sales decreased 15.3% year-over-year to P$9,253 million, mainly impacted by negative currency translation effects from the appreciation of the Mexican peso against the U.S. dollar. In the U.S. and Canada, net sales declined 14.5% year-over-year, reflecting the 3.0% decline in volume, unfavorable foreign currency effects, and a more competitive environment. During the same period, net sales in Mexico decreased 9.3% year-over-year, reflecting the sale of b:oost. On an organic basis, net sales in Mexico decreased 6.4%, reflecting a less favorable brand mix and a more promotional environment. Net sales in the RoW region decreased 25.1%, reflecting lower volume and unfavorable foreign exchange translation into Mexican pesos.
Net Sales by Category 3Q26 (in P$, millions)

Net sales of ‘Jose Cuervo’ decreased 21.3% compared to the same period of 2025, representing 32.1% of total net sales for the third quarter of 2026. Net sales of ‘Other Tequilas’ brands decreased 6.7% year-over-year, accounting for 43.3% of the total net sales. ‘Other Spirits’ brands represented 16.3% of total net sales and decreased 23.3% compared to the third quarter of 2025. ‘Non-alcoholic and Other’ contributed 2.8% of total net sales, decreasing 22.0% compared to the prior year period. ‘RTD’ represented 5.6%, with an 8.3% decrease in net sales compared to the previous year.

The gross margin decrease was largely due to unfavorable foreign currency effects from the appreciation of the Mexican peso against the U.S. dollar, an unfavorable geographic mix and a heavier promotional environment. This was partially offset by stable input costs. Adjusting for FX, the gross margin would have decreased 330 basis points, from 56.1% to 52.8%.

AMP expenses decreased 6.6% to P$1,986 million compared to the third quarter of 2025. As a percentage of net sales, AMP increased to 21.5% from 19.5% in the same period of the previous year. On a YTD basis, AMP represented 20.2% of net sales, in line with the Company’s full-year guidance range of 19% to 21%.

Distribution expenses decreased 8.2% to P$447 million compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by lower volume. As a percentage of net sales, distribution expenses increased to 4.8% from 4.5% in the same period of the previous year, due to operational deleveraging.

SG&A expenses increased 3.3% to P$1,179 million compared to the third quarter of 2025. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A increased to 12.7% from 10.4% in the same period of the previous year, due to operational deleveraging driven by the decline in net sales value.

Operating margin decreased by 1,660-basis points to 12.0%, down from 28.6% in the same period of 2025. This decrease was mainly due to a gross margin contraction, operational deleveraging, and the P$753 million gain in other income recorded in the third quarter of 2025, which primarily resulted from the sale of our b:oost brand and contractual settlements related to U.S. distribution agreements. Excluding non-recurring gains from 2025, operating margin would have decreased 800 basis points, from 21.7% in 2025 to 13.7% in 2026, adjusting for FX.

The EBITDA margin decreased by 1,600-basis points to 15.7% versus 31.7% in the same period of 2025. Excluding the P$753 million gain in other income recorded in the third quarter of 2025, the EBITDA margin would have decreased 760 basis points, from 24.8% in 2025 to 17.2% in 2026, on a constant currency basis.

The net financial result recorded an expense of P$256 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to an expense of P$24 million in the same period of 2025. The variation was primarily driven by a foreign exchange loss of P$152 million, reflecting the depreciation of the Mexican peso against the U.S. dollar during the quarter (compared to a gain of P$188 million in the third quarter of 2025), partially offset by lower interest expense, reflecting the reduction in debt.

Consolidated net income in the third quarter of 2026 decreased 84.6% to P$633 million, compared to P$4,123 million in the same period of 2025. This was mainly driven by a decrease in operating income and the gain from the sale of our equity interest in Lalo Spirits Holdings, Inc. recorded under the equity method in the third quarter of 2025, partially offset by lower income taxes. Excluding the gain from the sale of our equity interest in Lalo Spirits Holdings, Inc. and other income recorded in the third quarter of 2025, net margin would have decreased 790 basis points, from 15.9% to 8.0%, on a FX adjusted basis. Earnings per share (EPS) were P$0.18 pesos.

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were P$11,190 million (a decrease of P$842 million versus the same period of the previous year , mainly reflecting the US$100 million prepayment of our syndicated loan in the fourth quarter of 2025 and investments in associates). Total financial debt stood at P$19,029 million pesos (a decrease of P$2,306 million pesos versus the same period of the previous year).
During the third quarter of 2026, the Company generated P$1,015 million in net cash from operating activities and deployed P$199 million in investing activities.
Net cash from financing activities amounted to P$321 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net cash used of P$234 million in the same period of the previous year.
I FRS 9; IFRIC 16: Net investment hedge disclosures
Financial instruments to hedge net investments in foreign operations

Effective January 1 st, 2020, the Company designated its US$500 million Senior Notes due 2025 as a hedging instrument for its net investment in Sunrise Spirits Holdings, Inc., with the objective of mitigating the exchange rate risk arising between the functional currency of these operations and the functional currency of the holding company that has such investment. However, on September 27 th, 2021, the Company announced a cash tender offer and a consent solicitation to the holders of outstanding 2025 Senior Notes in circulation. The Company paid a total principal amount of US$346.6 million (Ps7,202 million) of the 2025 Senior Notes (69.3% of the original issuance of US$500 million). Therefore, the coverage designated by this bond is US$153.4 million (Ps3,192 million).

On October 31 st, 2021, the Company designated a new hedge in the amount of US$346.6 million (Ps7,202 million), which is part of the Company's US$800 million Senior Notes due 2031, as a hedging instrument for its net investment in Sunrise Spirits Holdings, Inc.

On August 31 st, 2022, the Company designated a new hedge in the amount of US$150 million (Ps2,999 million), which is part of the Company's US$800 million Senior Notes due 2031, as a hedging instrument for its net investment in Sunrise Spirits Holdings, Inc.

On September 30th, 2024, the Company designated a new hedge in the amount of US$150 million (Ps2,944 million), which is part of the Company's US$800 million Senior Notes due 2031, as a hedging instrument for its net investment in Sunrise Spirits Holdings, Inc.
The total coverage established by the Company is US$800 million.

The Company formally designated and documented the hedging relationship, setting the objectives, risk-hedging strategy, identification of the hedging instrument, hedged item, nature of the risk to be hedged, and effectiveness assessment methodology. Since the exchange rate hedging relationship is clear, the method the Company used to assess the effectiveness consisted of a qualitative effectiveness test by comparing the critical terms between the hedging instruments and the hedged items.
Net investment hedge in a foreign operation

The Company applies hedge accounting to the foreign exchange risk resulting from its investments in foreign operations because of changes in exchange rates arising between the functional currency of that operation and the functional currency of the holding company, regardless of whether the investment is held directly or through a sub-holder. The change in exchange rates is recognized in Other Comprehensive Income as part of the translation effect when the foreign operation is consolidated.

To this end, the Company designates the debt denominated in foreign currency as hedging instruments; therefore, the exchange effects arising from such debt are recognized in Other Comprehensive Income, in the translation effects line, to the extent that the hedge is effective. When the hedge is not effective, exchange rate differences are recognized in foreign exchange gain or loss in the consolidated income statement.

EBITDA is a measure used in the Company’s financial analysis that is not recognized under IFRS but is calculated from amounts that derive from the Company’s financial statements. We calculate EBITDA as net income plus depreciation and amortization, income tax expense, and interest expense, less interest income, plus foreign exchange gain (loss).

EBITDA is not an IFRS measure of liquidity or performance, nor is EBITDA a recognized financial measure under IFRS. We believe that EBITDA can be useful to facilitate comparisons of operating performance between periods on a combined basis, but these metrics may be calculated differently by other issuers. EBITDA should not be construed as an alternative to (i) net income as an indicator of the Company’s operating performance or (ii) cash flow from operating activities as a measure of the Company’s liquidity.
